title: High-Throughput PCR Amplification of MLST Loci Using a One-Pot Approach
author: Khaled Abdrabo

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: In a reagent reservoir for a 96‑well plate, combine the following per reaction and then multiply by 96 wells with a 10 % excess (1.1× total volume): 0.5 µL (48 µL → 55 µL) of each 10 µM primer (X‑Forward, X‑Reverse, Y‑Forward, Y‑Reverse, Z‑Forward, Z‑Reverse), 25 µL (2 400 µL → 2 750 µL) PowerPol 2X PCR Master Mix, and 17.5 µL (1 680 µL → 1 925 µL) ddH₂O. Adjust ddH₂O volume as needed so the final reaction volume reaches 50 µL per well.

steps.title: Dispense master mix into plate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel micropipette, dispense 45.5 µL of the prepared PCR master mix into each well of a 96‑well PCR plate.

steps.title: Add barcode primers
steps.instruction: Aliquot 1.5 µL of the selected barcode primers into each well containing the master mix.

steps.title: Add DNA template
steps.instruction: Add 3 µL of DNA template to each well (volume may be adjusted according to DNA quality and concentration) to obtain a final reaction volume of 50 µL per well.

steps.title: Seal and label plate
steps.instruction: Seal the 96‑well PCR plate with sealing film and clearly label the plate with sample ID, date, and experiment name.

steps.title: Run PCR program
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plate in a thermal cycler and run the following program: 1) Initial denaturation: 95 °C for 180 s (1 cycle). 2) MLST loci amplification (25 cycles): 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 15 s (annealing temperature should be optimized for each primer set), 72 °C 30 s. 3) Barcoding (10 cycles): 95 °C 15 s, 65 °C 15 s, 72 °C 30 s. 4) Final extension: 72 °C for 60 s (1 cycle). 5) Hold at 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Execute automated cleaning
steps.instruction: Subject the PCR plate to the automated cleaning program (Program No. 10) using the prescribed instrument settings.

steps.title: Add NG dye to new plate
steps.instruction: Prepare an 8‑well strip with approximately 150 µL of 10× NG dye per well. Using a multichannel micropipette, dispense 2 µL of NG dye into each well of a fresh 96‑well PCR plate.

steps.title: Mix and centrifuge plate
steps.instruction: Gently mix the plate contents by brief shaking or tapping (avoid vigorous mixing). Then briefly centrifuge the plate in a 96‑well plate centrifuge to collect the reaction mixture at the bottom of the wells.

steps.title: Cast agarose gel with tray
steps.instruction: Use a high‑throughput casting tray with two combs to cast an agarose gel containing 25 wells per comb (total 25 wells after solidification). Prior to casting, wet the tray and combs with TBE buffer to prevent sticking and facilitate removal for imaging.

steps.title: Prepare loading‑dye mapping
steps.instruction: Transfer PCR products to a 96‑well dye plate using the following alternating pattern: A1→A1, A2→B1, A3→A2, A4→B2, etc., so that each column of the PCR plate is distributed across the first two columns of the dye plate. Only the first two columns will later be loaded with a multichannel pipette; the third column will be loaded with a single‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Load samples onto gels
steps.instruction: Reserve one well per gel for a DNA ladder, leaving 24 wells for samples. Load the first column of the PCR plate into the first gel column using a multichannel pipette, repeat for the second column. Load the third column sequentially with a single‑channel pipette. Continue the pattern (two multichannel columns, one single‑channel column) for all columns. Each 96‑well PCR plate can be loaded onto four gels (24 samples per gel).

steps.title: Run gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the agarose gel at 110 V for 35 minutes.

steps.title: Visualize gel under UV
steps.instruction: Place the gel on a UV transilluminator and visualize to assess PCR amplification success.

steps.title: Set up ZiXpress bead cleanup
steps.instruction: On a ZiXpress 32 96‑well plate, fill wells as follows (leave well 5 empty): add variable volume of BeaverBeads™ DNA Select according to amplicon size, 50 µL PCR product, 400 µL 75 % ethanol, 50 µL DEPC‑treated water, and 400 µL ddH₂O. Each ZiXpress plate holds up to 16 PCR products (8 × 2 layout). Two plates can be processed simultaneously; a full 96‑well PCR plate requires three sequential cleaning runs.

steps.title: Mix and centrifuge after cleanup
steps.instruction: Gently mix the cleaned plate (brief shaking or tapping) and briefly centrifuge to collect the liquid at the bottom of the wells.
